alex: Hey infra team — onboarding heavy customer in germanywestcentral. We need a landing-zone VNet + NAT capacity. Requirements: /22 for node pools (k8s), separate /28 for PrivateLink/Private Endpoints, and bump in public IP quota for NAT so we can have 3 NAT gateways (autoscale pattern). Also we need A100 GPU quota increase for the same subscription (urgent for training jobs).

maria: Can you paste the subscription ID + tenant? also which resource group/name you plan to use for the NAT gateways?

alex: Subscription: 0f3a2b7c-9d4e-4c1b-8a0e-e9f7c1b2d5a6, Tenant: a1b2c3d4-1111-2222-3333-444455556666. RG will be obs-cust-gnrl-42-network. VNet name: obs-cust-gnrl-42-vnet.

trevor: reco for cidr + route: give two node subnets and one infra subnet. Example plan: 
- 10.40.0.0/22 -> VNet 
- 10.40.0.0/23 -> k8s-pool-1 (autoscale) 
- 10.40.2.0/23 -> k8s-pool-2 (GPU nodes) 
- 10.40.4.0/28 -> privatelink-endpoints
Use a dedicated route table for k8s to avoid SNAT hairpin.

Terraform snippet for the privatelink subnet:```hcl
resource "azurerm_subnet" "privatelink" {
  name                 = "privatelink-subnet"
  resource_group_name  = var.rg
  virtual_network_name = azurerm_virtual_network.vnet.name
  address_prefixes     = ["10.40.4.0/28"]
  service_endpoints    = ["Microsoft.Storage"]
}
```

and az cli to create NAT gateway with a public IP prefix (recommended):```bash
az network public-ip prefix create -g obs-cust-gnrl-42-network -n nat-pfx --location germanywestcentral --length 28
az network nat gateway create -g obs-cust-gnrl-42-network -n ngw-01 --public-ip-prefix nat-pfx --idle-timeout 10 --zone 1
```

raj: FYI Azure has a quota on Public IPs and Public IP Prefixes per subscription. You'll need the subscription-level increase for both: "Public IP addresses" and "Public IP Prefixes". Also check "Regional vNet peerings" if you're planning hub-spoke. For PrivateLink (Private Endpoint) there's a limit of private endpoints per subscription per region too. Raising that is separate.

raj: If you want to reduce public IP count: share NAT gateways across spokes using route tables + user-defined routes, or use a single NAT gateway per zone with Public IP Prefix to allow autoscale without needing many individual IPs.

infra-bot: Created support request SR# 2026-GL-89421 for Public IP / Prefix quota increases (subscription 0f3a2b7c). Assigned to Azure quota team.

azure-support-bot: Acknowledged SR# 2026-GL-89421 — target response 24h. Please attach business justification and expected sustained vCPU/GPU and outbound throughput.

maria: Also we need the GPU quota request — I'll open a companion SR for A100 (type: Standard_ND A100 or similar). Alex, how many GPUs do you need initially?

alex: Start with 16 A100s (8 in each k8s-pool), burst to 32 later. I'll add justification: training/benchmark runs + inference hot standby.

alex: Opened SR# 2026-GL-89430 for quota: A100 family increase in germanywestcentral (subscription 0f3a2b7c). Link: https://portal.azure.com/#blade/Microsoft_Azure_Support/ProblemReportsBlade/overview/id/2026-GL-89430

trevor: Temporary workaround while quotas are pending: schedule mixed nodepools — use NVv4 / NCas_T4 for low-cost baseline and mark GPU pool as preemptible/spot for short training runs. Also consider spreading across neighboring region (westeurope) if latency/sovereignty allows.

raj: Note about NAT: if k8s uses IP masquerade, check SNAT ports per NAT gateway. For high pod density we can hit SNAT exhaustion even if public IP quota is fine. Recommend enabling multiple public IPs on NAT gateway (prefix) and configuring kube-proxy/ip-masq appropriately.

maria: Action items: alex to attach business justification to both SRs, trevor to prepare TF plan + route tables, raj to draft SNAT guidance snippet, infra-bot to track SRs and notify channel on status.

alex: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
